1: # Vantage-ARS
2: 
3: The public website and founder-controlled, AI-staffed office for Vantage-ARS
4: ([vantage-ars.co.za](https://vantage-ars.co.za)): VoIP, networking and IT
5: infrastructure support, South Africa.
6: 
7: Author: Juan-louw Greyling <juanlouw.greyling@gmail.com>
8: 
9: ## Stack
10: 
11: - TanStack Start + React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, Vite 8, Nitro 3
12: - Postgres: Neon (or any Postgres) when `DATABASE_URL` is set, otherwise embedded PGLite
13: - Better Auth (founder email and password), pdf-lib for quotes, Gmail SMTP for notices
14: - Ten AI staff, each with a fixed role, working a durable queue on their own cadence
15: - Nine productised services at published prices; eight can be sold and delivered unattended under a standing founder delegation (ART-13), while the engineer-delivered support plan remains human-gated
16: 
17: ## What is in it
18: 
19: | Area                | Routes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
20: | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
21: | Public site         | `/`, `/services`, `/services/voip`, `/services/networking`, `/services/it-infrastructure`, `/services/ai-automation`, `/services/managed-support`, `/services/cloud-email`, `/services/security`, `/services/backup-recovery`, `/find`, `/assess`, `/automation`, `/guides`, `/rates`, `/work`, `/support`, `/status`, `/terms`, `/privacy` |
22: | Customer quote link | `/q/<token>`: view, download PDF, accept or decline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
23: | Founder office      | `/office`: command, autonomy, approvals, sales, ledger, customer book, site signals, chat, audit, metrics and more                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
24: | Founder governance  | `/office/delegations` (standing delegation), `/office/governance` (rulings, section 71 gates, signed receipts), `/office/revenue` (subscriptions, billing, customer mail), `/office/customers` (the customer book)                                                                                                                          |
25: | Operations          | `/status` (public readiness), `/api/health` (liveness), `/api/cron/floor` (scheduled run), `/api/ai/status`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
26: 
27: ## The office runs itself
28: 
29: With `AUTONOMY=on` and a `CRON_SECRET`, ten agents work a durable queue every
30: ten minutes. Each has named duties on their own cadence: reception classifies
31: enquiries, marketing scores leads on what the buyer actually wrote, flags repeat
32: site interest as prospects, and drafts weekly owned-channel campaigns, then files
33: a founder-gated handoff when demand is real; sales drafts real follow-ups on real
34: quotes, the service desk drafts acknowledgements, technical writes procedures,
35: finance chases overdue invoices, bills the subscriptions that are due and duns
36: the ones that are not, admin checks the filing and reviews the recurring-revenue
37: book, the orchestrator briefs you once a day from the books, and compliance halts
38: the office if the audit chain ever fails to verify. It also reminds the founder
39: weekly when an approval has waited a week; it never approves one on a timer.
40: 
41: None of them email a customer, spend money, win or lose a customer, or publish
42: anything. Those are founder approvals, with the constitutional trace attached —
43: unless you have granted a standing delegation.
44: 
45: Full detail, including every duty and every brake: **[docs/autonomy.md](docs/autonomy.md)**.
46: 
47: ## Standing delegation (ART-13)
48: 
49: Nothing is delegated by default. The office ships with no delegation at all, and
50: it stops at the founder gate for every cost, every customer win, every customer
51: loss and every marketing-to-sales handoff.
52: 
53: A delegation is the founder answering a whole class of question in advance:
54: "for this bounded class of action, at this price, up to this many times a day,
55: you may act without asking me again." It names the action kinds it covers, the
56: published rate lines it may charge, the most any single action may be worth, and
57: how many actions it may take per day and per month. It is revocable, and
58: revocation takes effect on the very next action.
59: 
60: A delegation never overrides a hard block. It cannot widen an agent's role,
61: permit a price that is not published, permit a promise to a customer, or survive
62: a halt. Every action taken under one is written into the audit chain against the
63: delegation that allowed it.
64: 
65: The founder sets it at **`/office/delegations`**. Four presets are offered, and
66: none of them is on until it is saved.
67: 
68: ## Productised services and recurring revenue
69: 
70: Nine services are published with a fixed scope, a fixed price and a
71: deliverable the office can produce from its own records: the managed support
72: plan and the remote health and spend watch, both monthly; the quarterly
73: infrastructure review; and the service report, the billing and rate compliance
74: audit, the infrastructure documentation and handover pack, the business
75: continuity plan, the service level and response review and the fault pattern
76: and incident review, all one-off.
77: 
78: Because the office can deliver them and can bill them, they are recurring
79: revenue rather than jobs. A subscription bills on its own cycle, the
80: deliverable is compiled from the office's own records, and the customer is sent
81: their report and their invoice. Every email the office sends is kept in full
82: under `customer_notices`.
83: 
84: None of it happens on its own. The office delivers and bills a plan only under
85: a delegation, and emails a customer only under a delegation that allows mail.
86: The book is at **`/office/revenue`**; the plans and their prices are on
87: **`/rates`** and **`/services/managed-support`**.
88: 
89: The customer book at **`/office/customers`** assembles every company the office
90: has actually touched — enquiry, lead, opportunity, invoice, receipt and
91: subscription — into one account with its status, open balance and monthly value.
92: It exports the book as CSV. It does not invent a customer from a page view.
93: 
94: Autonomous quoting, subscription start, recurring billing and fulfilment are
95: limited to plans the office can deliver from its own records without human
96: labour. The managed support plan includes engineer hours, so it is not sold or
97: billed unattended even if a delegation includes its rate.
98: 
99: Support time is logged at **`/office/service`** against the account, with the
100: minutes, a note and the work date. A service report uses that recorded time when
101: it exists and falls back to the one-hour-per-fault estimate, labelled as an
102: estimate, when it does not. The ledger journal and the combined audit/decision
103: chain also export as formula-safe CSV.
104: 
105: The governance record at **`/office/governance`** brings together the founder's
106: precedent rulings, section 71 gate records and signed execution receipts. Each
107: receipt signature is checked at read time; an approval that was skipped stays
108: visibly undecided at the gate. Ctrl/⌘ K opens office-wide search across the
109: founder snapshot — customers, approvals, tickets, money records, decisions and
110: pages — without exposing a public index.
111: 
112: **`/find`** asks three plain questions — the problem, the impact and the horizon
113: — and recommends a published service, the guides that explain it and a short
114: checklist before an enquiry. It recommends; it does not quote or promise an
115: outcome.
116: 
117: **`/assess`** is a browser-only IT readiness self-assessment across seven
118: operational practices. It separates unknowns from answers a visitor can assess,
119: and links improvement areas to existing service lines. It is not a technical
120: audit, security test or compliance certification; answers are not submitted or
121: saved unless the visitor explicitly attaches a short summary to a quote request.
122: That request offers the published initial remote assessment (up to 60 minutes);
123: scope and VAT treatment are confirmed in writing before any work starts.
124: 
125: **`/automation`** is a browser-only workflow planning checklist. It considers
126: repeat frequency, process clarity, information quality, known exceptions,
127: impact of errors and human approval controls, then distinguishes a bounded
128: pilot candidate from workflows that need controls first. The result is
129: deterministic, not AI-generated advice. Visitors can copy or download a local
130: pilot brief, or explicitly attach it to a written-scope quote request; it is not
131: sent unless the visitor submits the enquiry.
132: 
133: **`/services/ai-automation`** describes five human-led engagements: workflow
134: readiness review, agent blueprint, supervised workflow pilot, read-only
135: diagnostics pilot and governance/operations pack. Every engagement is scoped
136: and quoted using applicable published labour rates; model and software fees
137: remain separate. Diagnostics use customer-authorized read-only data;
138: production access, system scans, unattended actions and ongoing monitoring are
139: not included by default.
140: 
141: Marketing at **`/office/marketing`** also shows the last thirty days of real
142: site signals: page views by day, top pages, referral sources, countries and the
143: latest events. The record holds no IP address, no cookie and no inferred
144: identity; anonymous site signals are not a cold-contact list. Paid campaign
145: proposals are capped at R300 per Johannesburg calendar month, still require
146: founder approval, and cannot launch ads until an advertising account is
147: connected.
148: 
149: ## Run locally
150: 
151: Node 22.12 or newer.
152: 
153: ```sh
154: npm ci
155: cp .env.example .env      # fill in what you need; everything is optional locally
156: npm run dev               # http://localhost:8080
157: npm run validate          # typecheck + lint + tests
158: npm run verify:office     # boots a real office and proves it runs autonomously
159: ```
160: 
161: `npm run verify:office` is the one that matters. It starts a real embedded
162: Postgres, files the records the public site would really file, runs the real
163: scheduler, and asserts on what the real agents did — 243 checks, no mocks and
164: no sample data. If autonomy breaks, this fails.
165: 
166: ## Environment
167: 
168: Everything is in [`.env.example`](.env.example). The ones that matter:
169: 
170: | Variable                                                            | Purpose                                                                              |
171: | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
172: | `DATABASE_URL`                                                      | Postgres (Neon). Migrations run during `npm run build`. Unset means embedded PGLite. |
173: | `PGLITE_DATA_DIR`                                                   | With PGLite, keep data here. Unset means in-memory, lost on restart.                 |
174: | `BETTER_AUTH_URL`                                                   | The public URL.                                                                      |
175: | `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`                                                | A long random secret (`openssl rand -base64 32`). Required in production.            |
176: | `FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN`                                               | One-time code for creating the founder account. Remove it afterwards.                |
177: | `FOUNDER_EMAIL`                                                     | The only account allowed into the office.                                            |
178: | `AUTONOMY`                                                          | `on` lets the office act unattended. Anything else and only the button works.        |
179: | `CRON_SECRET`                                                       | Bearer token the scheduler must present. 16+ characters.                             |
180: | `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_FROM` | Optional outbound mail over implicit TLS (port 465); use a provider-verified sender. |
181: | `GMAIL_SMTP_USER`, `GMAIL_SMTP_APP_PASSWORD`                        | Legacy Gmail fallback; messages use the Gmail account as sender.                     |
182: | `FOUNDER_WEBHOOK_URL`                                               | Optional HTTPS webhook for the same founder notices (Slack, Discord or generic).     |
183: | `PAYMENT_*`                                                         | Bank details on the site and quotes.                                                 |
184: | `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` / `XAI_API_KEY`     | AI staff reasoning. Every autonomous duty works without it.                          |
185: 
186: Nothing new is needed for the delegation or the productised services. A
187: delegation is set inside the office. Generic SMTP supports a verified
188: `hello@vantage-ars.co.za` sender; the legacy Gmail fallback continues to send
189: from the configured Gmail account. Set up the provider mailbox and publish its
190: SPF/DKIM records before switching the sender.
191: 
192: ## Founder setup (once)
193: 
194: 1. Set `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN` and, if needed, `FOUNDER_EMAIL`. Deploy.
195: 2. Open `/office`. The page offers "First-time founder setup".
196: 3. Enter the founder email, a password of 12+ characters and the setup token.
197: 4. Remove `FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN` and redeploy. Sign-up is closed once a founder exists.
198: 
199: ## Final launch verification
200: 
201: Before you brand the project live, run the final launch gate:
202: 
203: ```sh
204: npm run final:check
205: ```
206: 
207: This enforces the production deployment checks and then runs the repo-wide
208: verification pass (`typecheck`, lint and the real office tests). It is the
209: single final gate before pushing to production.
210: 
211: ## Next steps
212: 
213: The execution roadmap for turning this into a live, revenue-generating operation is in
214: [docs/next-steps.md](docs/next-steps.md). It covers launch, monitoring,
215: research/AI expansion, marketing, recurring revenue, and the governance guardrails that keep the office safe.
216: 
217: ## Deploy
218: 
219: **[docs/deploy-vercel.md](docs/deploy-vercel.md) is the full walkthrough** — the
220: variables to set, the founder setup, the domain cutover, and how to verify it.
221: 
222: ### Vercel + Neon (recommended)
223: 
224: 1. Import the GitHub repo in Vercel.
225: 2. Add a Neon database and set `DATABASE_URL`, then the auth settings above.
226: 3. Set `AUTONOMY=on` and a generated `CRON_SECRET`. The ten-minute tick is
227:    scheduled by the `office-scheduler` GitHub Actions workflow — add the same
228:    `CRON_SECRET` as a repository secret (Settings → Secrets and variables →
229:    Actions) so the scheduler call authenticates. GitHub's cron is best-effort
230:    on quiet repositories, so the office also nudges itself: a hit on
231:    `/api/health` or a real page view starts a catch-up tick when the last one
232:    is over ten minutes old. `vercel.json` keeps a daily run as the final
233:    fallback (Vercel's Hobby plan rejects crons more often than daily).
234: 4. Deploy. `npm run build` applies migrations.
235: 5. Check `https://www.vantage-ars.co.za/api/health` — `scheduler.overdue` should
236:    be `false`.
237: 
238: ### Docker (any server)
239: 
240: ```sh
241: cp .env.example .env      # set AUTONOMY=on, CRON_SECRET, auth settings
242: docker compose up -d --build
243: ```
244: 
245: The compose file also starts a `scheduler` sidecar that ticks
246: `/api/cron/floor` every ten minutes with your `CRON_SECRET`, so an unattended
247: server never depends on GitHub Actions cron.
248: 
249: ### Plain Node
250: 
251: ```sh
252: npm ci && npm run build && npm start      # .output/server/index.mjs, PORT defaults to 3000
253: ```
254: 
255: For an always-on server without Docker, `deploy/systemd/` ships a service unit
256: plus a timer that ticks the floor every ten minutes.
257: 
258: ## Operations
259: 
260: **Health.** `GET /api/health` answers "is the business running?" — database,
261: audit chain, scheduler freshness, work queue, mail delivery, and the money
262: position. It returns 503 when something that matters is wrong, and never exposes
263: a secret or a customer. Sign in and it returns the full picture. Hitting it also
264: nudges a stale scheduler back on cadence, so an uptime monitor doubles as the
265: heartbeat.
266: 
267: **Public status.** `/status` is a readiness check, not an uptime page: five
268: lines read from the office at the moment it loads — records, decision-record
269: integrity, scheduled work, published-rate agreement and founder control. The
270: full health document is reduced on the server, so money, customers, the halt
271: reason and delegation limits never reach a visitor. It keeps no history and
272: makes no availability promise.
273: 
274: **Autonomy UI.** `/office` shows the scheduler state, every duty and when it is
275: next due, the live queue, and what each agent did last. The same panel runs the
276: office on demand through the identical code path. It also lists the
277: dead-letter queue on its own, with the error that killed each item, and lets
278: the founder redrive one: redriving is a founder action, never an automatic one,
279: and it is written to the audit chain.
280: 
281: **Money.** Amounts are integer cents. A receipt may only retire money actually
282: owed — the balance update and the ledger row are one transaction that reads the
283: receivable under lock. A quote's figure is generated from the published rate
284: card, never from agent prose.
285: 
286: **Audit chain.** Every decision and every event is hash-chained in one
287: transaction under an advisory lock, so the chain cannot fork. SEAL verifies the
288: whole chain twice a day and halts the office if it fails. `/office/audit` shows
289: the result.
290: 
291: **Backup.** `/office/audit` exports every business table as JSON with a SHA-256
292: checksum, including live customer quote links. Restore is add-only and
293: transactional: it never deletes or overwrites, and a half-restored office is
294: impossible.
295:

297: 
298: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs typecheck, lint, tests, a production build and
299: the office verification on every push to `main` and every pull request.

313: ## Governance
314: 
315: Agents act only inside their role. Anything that costs money, risks a customer,
316: or can win one goes to the founder for approval, unless a standing delegation
317: covers it. Every decision is recorded in a hash-chained audit trail that the
318: office verifies on its own.
319: 
320: The founder's own rulings are recorded too, and in more detail than the chain
321: alone: the risk tier of the decision, the POPIA section 71 test and its
322: answers, the material conditions the ruling was made under, and a signed
323: receipt for the execution. A precedent is evidence, never authority — nothing
324: in the code reads a past approval to permit a present action.
325: 
326: How the office is bounded, and what it does not do:
327: **[docs/governance-architecture.md](docs/governance-architecture.md)**.
